Check yourself. 1. Expected income $40,000. Payout at 70%? The answer: $28,000/yr (~$2,333/month).
Check yourself. 2. What's the retained 30% for? The answer: Absorbing expected losses and bad years without cutting into principal.
Check yourself. 3. Realised income lags expected for two quarters. What happens? The answer: Cut the payout to the policy share of the new realised level.
The payout policy: how much you can take out.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to set a payout you can sustain through bad years, and the rules that change it.
